title: Conclave project profile
description: Per-project description of the components, stacks, checks and gates the Conclave team works with. Lives at .claude/conclave.json in the project.

name.description: Project name as the agents should call it.

base.description: Git ref every diff, coverage gate and audit compares against (e.g. origin/main).

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the project is and who runs it. Shown to every agent.

components.description: Independently buildable parts of the project. One dev and one challenger run per touched component.

paths.description: Directory prefixes (end with /) or globs this component owns. Used to route findings to the right dev.

tests.description: Directories or globs where tests live. Challengers and the test engineer may only write here.

stacks.description: Stack packs (skills/stack-<name>) the roles load for this component.

ui.description: True when the component renders a user interface; adds the ux role as consultant and reviewer.

checks.description: Fast checks the dev runs before reporting, in order (lint, typecheck, unit tests). Shell commands run from the repo root.

build.description: Full build commands QA runs (e.g. cmake --build, npm run build).

e2e.description: Slow end-to-end suites QA runs after the fast checks.

command.description: Produces a Cobertura XML or lcov report.

report.description: Path of the report the command writes, relative to the repo root.

src_root.description: Passed to diff-cover --src-root when report paths are relative to a subdirectory.

include.description: Globs limiting which files the gate judges (e.g. logic modules only).

setup.description: Commands that make checks runnable when the environment is cold (venv creation, npm ci). Agents run these only when a check fails for a missing tool.

pitfalls.description: Things this codebase gets wrong under pressure. Fed verbatim to the dev, challenger and reviewers.

conventions.description: Project rules beyond CLAUDE.md that reviewers enforce (layering, naming, migration policy).

contracts.description: Pairs of component names that talk to each other through an interface the architect must specify and the devs cross-check.

stakes.description: What a severity-high defect does to a real user of this project. Completes the sentence 'high = ...'.

threat_model.description: Who the attacker is, what they can reach, and what must never leak.

secrets.description: Names of secrets or tokens that must never appear in logs, tests or fixtures.

paths.description: Files and directories the docs-writer owns.

roadmap.description: File that holds the todo list or roadmap table, if any.

paths.description: CI, container, packaging and release files the devops role owns.

ci.description: Path of the CI definition, e.g. .github/workflows/ci.yml.

release.description: Files whose version fields must be bumped together on release.

coverage_changed_lines.description: Minimum percent of added or modified lines that must be covered. Omit to disable the gate.

flake_runs.description: How many times QA re-runs changed test files to catch flakes.

extra.description: Additional gate commands; non-zero exit is red.

mutation_probes.description: The test-auditor sabotages the implementation once per contract test and requires the test to fail; costly on compiled stacks.

scopes.description: Allowed conventional-commit scopes, if the project restricts them.

coauthor.description: Whether to add a Co-Authored-By trailer.

branch_prefix.description: Prefix for feature branches, e.g. dev/.

models.description: Per-role model overrides. Keys are role names (lead, pm, architect, dev, challenger, reviewer, refuter, test-engineer, qa, docs-writer, devops, ux) or the groups planners, workers, reviewers, mechanical.

min_tier.description: Never go below this tier for code changes.

always_review.description: Run reviewer-correctness even at T0 when a code file changes.

risky_paths.description: Paths that bump any task touching them to at least T2 (migrations, auth, payment, file deletion).

contract_by_default.description: Run T3 in contract mode (test-first contract tests, audited and frozen) unless the lead is told otherwise.

design_duel_by_default.description: Run T3 with a design duel (two dev designs, cross-critique, the architect judges) unless the lead is told otherwise.
